title: The Tip JRC mechanism makes an Agent's own capital absorb the first slice of every loss alone, for incentives and to avoid disputes
content:
A.3.2.1.2.2.1.2.1 defines the Tip JRC mechanism: "losses from a distinct risk event are first absorbed entirely by the Prime Agent's Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC), up to a specific threshold amount," the threshold being a percentage of Total JRC. A.3.2.1.2.2.1.2.2 handles the excess — allocated "pro-rata across the rest of the JRC capital," meaning remaining IJRC plus all external junior capital (PEJRC and TEJRC).

The Atlas states both reasons, and they are different in kind. The incentive reason: initial absorption solely by IJRC "ensures that Prime Agents are highly incentivized to prevent losses." Because external junior capital can be rented, an Agent could otherwise dilute its own exposure until small losses were mostly someone else's problem — the Tip restores full first-loss exposure regardless of how much external capital sits alongside it.

The administrative reason is the one that is easy to miss: it "avoids the need to resolve disputes regarding the allocation of small losses to EJRC providers." Loss attribution is expensive and contentious, and most losses are small. Making the Agent eat them unilaterally means the machinery for apportioning losses among capital providers only ever runs for events large enough to justify it.

The structural elegance is that the Tip is sized as a percentage of *Total* JRC, not of IJRC. An Agent that rents more external capital therefore raises its own absolute first-loss exposure proportionally — leverage and skin in the game scale together automatically, with no separate constraint needed.
description: Losses from a risk event hit Internal JRC exclusively up to a threshold set as a percentage of total JRC; only the excess is shared pro-rata with rented and tokenized external junior capital.
